study_identification.author_journal_year: Loreto et al., Alzheimer's & Dementia: Diagnosis, Assessment & Disease Monitoring, 2024
study_identification.title: Alzheimer's disease heterogeneity revealed by neuroanatomical normative modeling

study_characteristics.study_objective: The study aimed to assess neuroanatomical heterogeneity in a real-world clinical cohort of patients with confirmed Alzheimer's disease (AD) using normative modeling. It also aimed to explore individual-level anatomo-clinical correlations and the association between global amyloid burden and cortical thickness deviations.

site_effect_handling.reason: The paper describes using Hierarchical Bayesian Regression to handle multi-site data.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR) was used to model site effects. The model, pre-trained on a large multi-site reference cohort, was adapted to the clinical cohort's site using data from 20 local controls. HBR accounts for additive and multiplicative batch effects.
site_effect_handling_detail.reason: The paper and supplement provide details on the HBR method and the transfer learning approach.
site_effect_handling_detail.supporting_text: This model was then optimized using cortical thickness data from controls scanned at the same acquisition site as the clinical cohort (n = 20). This gives stable estimates of the transferred model parameters in an adapted transfer learning approach.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study uses Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR) specifically to handle nuisance effects from different sites. The supplementary material (Appendix 1) details how HBR addresses limitations of other methods by modeling site effects.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Hierarchical Bayesian regression proposed by Kia and colleagues was used, given its advantages over other methods for normative modeling of real-world clinical data. ... HBR is an effective means of addressing these limitations, primarily because it incorporates structural dependencies among model parameters by sharing a common prior distribution. ... it calculates z-statistics to account for both additive and multiplicative batch effects, obviating the need for data harmonization.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: This model was then optimized using cortical thickness data from controls scanned at the same acquisition site as the clinical cohort (n = 20). This gives stable estimates of the transferred model parameters in an adapted transfer learning approach.

deviation_metric.reason: The paper defines outliers based on z-scores and uses the total outlier count as a key metric.
deviation_metric.supporting_text: Here, z-scores of < -1.96 were defined as outliers... The total outlier count was calculated by summing the number of outlier regions for each patient.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: ANCOVA was used to test the effect of clinical groupings (sex, phenotype, disease stage, depression) on the total outlier count. Pearson correlation was used to test the association between outlier count and age. Linear regression was used to test the association between outlier count and amyloid burden (SUVR).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Brain atrophy in Alzheimer's disease is highly heterogeneous, and normative modeling can be used to explore individual anatomo-clinical correlations.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The superior temporal sulcus had the highest proportion of outliers (60%), but overall, atrophy patterns were very heterogeneous. The total outlier count was higher in non-amnestic patients, those with more advanced disease, and those without depression. A surprising negative association was found between amyloid burden and outlier count.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study had a small sample size, a mismatch in scanner/field strength between clinical and adaptation data, and limited clinical data due to its retrospective nature. The analysis was also limited to cortical regions, excluding subcortical structures.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Normative modeling can be used to investigate individual profiles of brain atrophy and their relationship to clinical presentation, allowing for a more personalized understanding of Alzheimer's disease.
